title: Ecology, evolution & key concepts
sub: Lecture 2 · Intro to ecology · glossary section 1
blurb: What ecology is, who founded it, natural selection, niche vs habitat.
h1: The basics everything else builds on
lede: Lecture 2 (Intro to ecology) plus section 1 of the glossary, Ecology in the Anthropocene. Short, but the exam loves the definitions and the Darwin vs Wallace story.
six: **Ecology** = how organisms interact with each other and their physical environment: why they live where they do, in the numbers they do.
The word comes from Greek **oîkos** (house) + **logía** (study of).
**Natural selection** needs three things: variation in traits, differential reproduction and heredity.
**Darwin** saw competition between individuals as the driving force of selection, **Wallace** saw the environment.
**Habitat** is where an organism lives; the **niche** is its role and requirements.
**Fundamental niche** = what physiology allows; **realized niche** = what it actually occupies with competitors and predators around.

questions.q: Which is the best definition of ecology?
questions.answer: The science of how organisms interact with each other and with their physical environment
wrong: The study of how traits are inherited from parents
The classification and naming of species
questions.e: Glossary 1a: ecology asks why organisms are distributed and abundant as they are, shaped by biotic and abiotic processes.

questions.q: The word ecology comes from Greek oîkos + logía. What does oîkos mean?
questions.e: oîkos = house, logía = study of: the study of the 'house' of living organisms.

questions.q: Which two ancient Greeks does the lecture name at the start of ecology?
Who is called the father of modern taxonomy and spoke of the 'economy of nature'?

questions.answer: A joint reading of Wallace's essay and Darwin's writings at the Linnean Society
wrong: Darwin published On the Origin of Species
questions.e: Darwin received Wallace's Ternate essay on 18 June 1858; the joint Linnean reading followed on 1 July. The Origin came out in 1859.

questions.q: According to the lecture, what did Wallace see as the main driving force of selection?
questions.e: Darwin stressed competition between individuals; Wallace stressed the environment.

questions.q: Which three ingredients does natural selection need?
questions.answer: Variation in traits, differential reproduction and heredity
questions.e: With all three, the favoured trait becomes more common in the population.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed in the glossary as a driver of evolution?
questions.e: Evolution is driven by mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, migration and recombination.

questions.q: Speciation usually happens when populations become…
questions.e: Gene flow between them is then strongly reduced or absent.

questions.q: How does true extinction differ from local extirpation?
questions.answer: In extinction no viable population remains anywhere
wrong: Extirpation is permanent, extinction is temporary
questions.e: Local extirpation is loss in one place; extinction means gone everywhere.

questions.q: A species could live on a whole mountain, but a competitor keeps it to the lower slopes. The lower slopes are its…
questions.e: Fundamental = set by physiology and resources; realized = what it actually occupies with competitors and predators.

questions.q: Habitat vs niche: which statement is right?
questions.answer: Habitat is where it lives; niche is its role and requirements
wrong: Habitat and niche mean the same
Niche is where it lives; habitat is its role
questions.e: Habitat = physical and biotic environment; niche = multidimensional role and requirements.

questions.q: Directional, stabilising and disruptive are three…
questions.e: Lecture 2 shows the three modes of selection.

questions.q: Animals whose body temperature mostly follows the environment are…
questions.e: Lecture 2: ectotherms vs endotherms, under the role of abiotic conditions (temperature).

questions.q: Galápagos finches and the animals of Madagascar are lecture examples of…
questions.e: Adaptive radiation: one lineage splits into many species filling different niches.

vocab.meaning: Science of how organisms interact with each other and their physical environment, and why they are distributed and abundant as they are.
Change in heritable characteristics of populations across generations (mutation, selection, drift, migration, recombination).
Heritable traits that raise survival or reproduction become more common because their carriers leave more offspring.
New species arise when populations become genetically different and reproductively isolated.
A species disappears when its last individuals die; no viable population is left anywhere.
Loss of a species in one place while it survives elsewhere.
The physical and biotic environment where an organism lives.
The species' multidimensional role and requirements: conditions, resources and interactions.
The niche set by physiology and resources alone.
The part of the niche actually occupied when competitors and predators are present.
How well an individual survives and reproduces compared with others.
A heritable trait that helps an organism survive or reproduce in its environment.
Selection for traits that help win mates.
One lineage splitting into many species that fill different niches (Galápagos, Madagascar).
An animal whose body heat comes mostly from the environment.
An animal that produces its own body heat.

facts: The word ecology comes from Greek oîkos, meaning {house|life|earth|nature}.
Linnaeus is called the father of modern {taxonomy|ecology|genetics|evolution}.
Darwin received Wallace's essay from {Ternate|Galápagos|Madagascar|Borneo} in 1858.
On the Origin of Species was published in {1859|1858|1871|1900}.
Wallace saw the {environment|competition|mate choice|climate} as the driving force of selection.
The niche a species actually occupies with competitors around is the {realized|fundamental|potential|keystone} niche.
Natural selection needs variation, differential reproduction and {heredity|migration|isolation|mutation}.
